title: Kepler Q1 to Q16 do not resolve a linear transit-contrast relation with fitted rotation brightness in KOI-2700
abstract: We test a contemporaneous linear relation between local dust-transit contrast and fitted rotation brightness in KOI-2700. Kepler release 25 gives 1217 selected orbits with 0.07-phase bands. The brightness model for each orbit uses other-parity orbits in the same quarter. Transit slopes are -13.2 ppm per brightness standard deviation in aperture flux and -7.7 in corrected flux. Approximate 95 percent cluster intervals include zero. A smooth model without transits produces slopes of -10.5 and -12.5 through local baseline curvature. Subtraction of the mean control contrast gives slopes of -0.7 and 3.9, with intervals of -21.3 to 19.5 and -21.9 to 29.4. Two other band widths and two other block lengths retain the differential null result. The corrections were added after inspection. Model errors, sample selection, long-lived noise and tail light loss in control bands limit the result. We do not rule out stellar activity effects, infer a dust supply law or find a new planet. Both products share photons. There is no independent-instrument confirmation. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Local contrast slopes versus fitted rotation brightness. Lines show approximate conditional 95 percent cluster intervals. The differential statistic subtracts the mean of two control contrasts. The two flux products share photons.
